data.name: Vishnu
data.gender_notes: Vishnu is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The god who preserves the universe through the maintenance of law and dharma. The name Vishnu carries the meaning “Preserver of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Vishnu usually hope their child will grow to embody preserver of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of the power of the universe to sustain and protect.
data.etymology: Vishnu belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Preserver of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vishnu total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Vishnu is deeply ingrained in the Hindu culture and represents one of the primary deities in the Hindu pantheon. Vishnu is symbolized by a blue-skinned being with four arms, carrying a conch shell, a discus, a mace, and the Sudarshan Chakra. He is also revered as the protector and preserver of the universe. Upon hearing the name Vishnu, it evokes a sense of protection, stability, and faith in the Hindu community.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Vishnu is considered the preserver of the universe and the sustainer of life. He upholds the principles of righteousness and harmony in the world, ensuring that order and balance are maintained. His spiritual significance lies in His role as the embodiment of love, compassion, and protection. He is also the source of unconditional love and a beacon of hope and faith for millions of Hindus worldwide. The chanting of Vishnu's holy names, such as Hare Krishna or Hare Rama, is believed to purify the mind and soul, leading one towards spiritual growth and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vishnu is the preserver in the Hindu trinity, symbolizing the sustaining force of the universe. His name derives from the Sanskrit word 'vis' meaning abode and 'nhu' meaning all pervading, reflecting His omnipresence.

vedic_reference.note: Vishnu is a central deity in Hinduism and is mentioned in various Vedic texts.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Vishnu remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.

name_in_real_life.story: Radha Vishnu from Bali, Indonesia embodies the meaning of Vishnu - "Preserver of the Universe". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.
